validation_version: TOEFL ITP Grammar Pipeline v1.1 Validation Batch

classification_legend.OBSERVED: Directly informed by the analyzed corpus/ranges; guidance only, not a quota.
classification_legend.DERIVED: Closed taxonomy or mechanism label derived from observed evidence.
classification_legend.HEURISTIC: Batch diversity/design choice; not an ETS standard or hard quota.

primary_target.note: Uses the closed taxonomy categories defined from OBSERVED corpus counts; batch allocation is a HEURISTIC spread, not a quota.

subtype.note: Names the exact construction within each closed primary_target, independently authored for this batch.

tested_error_type.note: Uses the closed 15-value mechanism vocabulary defined from OBSERVED taxonomy evidence.

sentence_length_target.note: Targets the OBSERVED section ranges and means while varying short, medium, and long items.

clause_count_target.note: Follows the OBSERVED one-/two-/three-clause shape approximately for each section.

distractor_type.note: Each Structure distractor is assigned one of the OBSERVED/closed tested_error_type mechanisms.

error_span_type.note: Uses the span-type vocabulary and diversity guidance derived from the OBSERVED Written Expression distribution.

error_scope.note: Uses the defined local/clause_level/sentence_level/cross_clause labels; the batch mix is HEURISTIC.

error_location.note: Randomized with a mild late/sentence_final emphasis based on the OBSERVED distribution.

difficulty.note: EASY/MEDIUM/HARD is assigned from syntax, dependency, span scope, and confusability; vocabulary rarity is not used.

correct_answer_position.note: Positions are spread across A-D using the OBSERVED near-even pattern without forcing a small-batch quota.

vocabulary_domain.note: Uses diverse academic/general-interest domains, following the OBSERVED diversity principle without reusing a source-domain roster.

primary_target.OBSERVED: The taxonomy defines a closed set of 15 primary_target values and reports section-level frequencies.
primary_target.DERIVED: Use one closed-taxonomy primary target per item and spread the batch across multiple categories.
primary_target.HEURISTIC: The 15-item allocation favors observed Structure categories while deliberately retaining low-frequency categories.

subtype.OBSERVED: The taxonomy documents representative construction subtypes within each primary target.
subtype.DERIVED: Name the exact construction being tested rather than inventing a new primary category.
subtype.HEURISTIC: Choose independently authored constructions with no reuse of source wording or distinctive facts.

difficulty.OBSERVED: Structure difficulty estimates cluster in the low-to-mid range, with syntax and distractor similarity as relevant features.
difficulty.DERIVED: Difficulty must come from syntax, dependency distance, construction rarity, and distractor similarity, not obscure vocabulary.
difficulty.HEURISTIC: Use a 4 EASY / 8 MEDIUM / 3 HARD split for this 15-item batch.

correct_answer_position.OBSERVED: The observed Structure correct positions are broadly balanced across A-D.
correct_answer_position.DERIVED: Long-run generated output should trend toward even A-D coverage.
correct_answer_position.HEURISTIC: Use A=4, B=4, C=4, D=3 in this small batch.

vocabulary_domain.OBSERVED: The observed Structure sample uses highly diverse academic and general-interest domains.
vocabulary_domain.DERIVED: Domain knowledge must not be needed to solve the grammar item.
vocabulary_domain.HEURISTIC: Use 15 distinct, plain academic/general-interest domains, one per item.

sentence_length_target.OBSERVED: Structure sentence lengths range from 10 to 27 words with a mean near 20.
sentence_length_target.DERIVED: Keep generated sentences within the observed range and centered on the observed band.
sentence_length_target.HEURISTIC: Mix short, medium, and long targets with a batch mean near 20 words.

clause_count_target.OBSERVED: Structure has approximately one-third one-clause items, one-half two-clause items, and a minority of three-plus-clause items.
clause_count_target.DERIVED: Use finite-clause count as a batch-level diversity control.
clause_count_target.HEURISTIC: Target 5 one-clause, 7 two-clause, and 3 three-or-more-clause items.

distractor_type.OBSERVED: The shared taxonomy defines 15 tested_error_type values; Structure most often uses missing, extra, order, and fragment mechanisms.
distractor_type.DERIVED: Every distractor must map to one closed tested_error_type and remain superficially plausible.
distractor_type.HEURISTIC: Favor dominant mechanisms while varying mechanisms across the 45 distractor slots.

primary_target.OBSERVED: The taxonomy defines a closed set of 15 primary_target values and reports Written Expression frequencies.
primary_target.DERIVED: Use one closed-taxonomy primary target per item and spread the batch across multiple categories.
primary_target.HEURISTIC: Favor reference/determiner, word-class, verb, complementation, nonfinite, and parallel targets while retaining broad coverage.

subtype.OBSERVED: The taxonomy documents representative construction subtypes within each primary target.
subtype.DERIVED: Name the exact construction containing the single planted error.
subtype.HEURISTIC: Author every sentence and error context independently from abstract rules only.

tested_error_type.OBSERVED: Written Expression errors are distributed across the shared 15-value tested_error_type vocabulary, with part-of-speech, verb-form, agreement, and preposition mechanisms prominent.
tested_error_type.DERIVED: Exactly one marked portion is erroneous, and its mechanism must map to the closed vocabulary.
tested_error_type.HEURISTIC: Use varied mechanisms with no fragment errors and with several local, clause-level, and cross-clause examples.

error_span_type.OBSERVED: Observed error spans cover noun_phrase, verb_phrase, adjective, prepositional_phrase, pronoun, relative_marker, and a long tail of additional span types.
error_span_type.DERIVED: Mark a natural grammatical span that requires sentence context to diagnose.
error_span_type.HEURISTIC: Distribute the 25 spans across the main span types and selected long-tail types.

error_scope.OBSERVED: Written Expression errors are most often local, followed by clause_level, with fewer sentence_level and cross_clause errors.
error_scope.DERIVED: Use scope to control detectability and ensure the other three marked portions remain correct.
error_scope.HEURISTIC: Target 14 local, 8 clause_level, 2 sentence_level, and 1 cross_clause item.

error_location.OBSERVED: Observed locations are slightly skewed toward late and sentence_final, with sentence_initial least common.
error_location.DERIVED: Randomize location rather than clustering errors in one position.
error_location.HEURISTIC: Use a mixed 25-item pattern with 2 sentence_initial, 4 early, 6 middle, 7 late, and 6 sentence_final locations.

difficulty.OBSERVED: Written Expression difficulty is driven by error scope, detectability, syntax, and plausibility rather than rare vocabulary.
difficulty.DERIVED: Keep all three dummy spans plausible and make the single error context-dependent.
difficulty.HEURISTIC: Use a 16 EASY / 7 MEDIUM / 2 HARD split for this 25-item batch.

correct_answer_position.OBSERVED: The observed error positions are broadly balanced, with a slight B-heavy pattern.
correct_answer_position.DERIVED: Long-run generated output should trend toward even A-D coverage.
correct_answer_position.HEURISTIC: Use A=7, B=6, C=6, D=6 in this small batch.

vocabulary_domain.OBSERVED: The observed Written Expression sample uses a wide range of academic and general-interest domains.
vocabulary_domain.DERIVED: Outside knowledge must not be required to locate or correct the error.
vocabulary_domain.HEURISTIC: Use 25 distinct domains, one per item, with familiar academic vocabulary.
